Hi Marissa — thanks for the summary, that looks right. A few clarifications from our side:

- Residency: We require EU residency for any PHI. If PHI is processed or temporarily stored outside the EU, that's a blocker unless we have explicit controls and contractual terms.
- Retention: The 7-year requirement applies to all records containing PHI, including application logs that could contain PII/PHI.
- Telemetry: We do not allow PHI to be sent to third-party analytics/telemetry vendors. If Observr captures logs that might include PHI, we need a configuration option to disable telemetry for our environment.
- Certifications: Procurement will need SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 evidence. HIPAA BAAs are important; please confirm if Redwood will sign a BAA.
- Marketplace flow: Procurement prefers purchasing through a cloud marketplace (GCP Marketplace) — can you confirm whether subscription/licensing and delegated billing are supported?

Procurement (cc'd) will follow up with a questionnaire; please assign a point of contact for legal/security.

Thanks,

Marissa / team — here are short answers you can send back to Alice + procurement. I attached the Observr SLA snapshot.

- Subprocessors (telemetry/logging): Observr Inc. — collects anonymized metrics and service telemetry (latency, error rates). We also use CloudProviderX (GCP) for compute/storage and a managed monitoring service for infra alerts. Full matrix attached (redwood_subprocessors_matrix.xlsx).

- Telemetry disable: Yes — customer-level telemetry can be disabled. Caveats: 1) Disabling telemetry removes aggregated metrics and some automated alerting; 2) SDK-level client logs may still be present unless you opt into our redaction feature. We can enable a strict redaction + telemetry-off profile for BlueSky so PHI is never forwarded to Observr.

- Residency & PHI: If you require EU-only processing for PHI, we recommend Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem). Dedicated (reserved capacity in EU region) can also meet residency if you require managed infra in the EU and contractual guarantees. Hosted API (multi-region) can be configured for EU-only data planes for certain customers, but for strict PHI use we recommend Dedicated or Private.

- Retention: Log retention is configurable per-tenant. We can set retention to 7 years for any log buckets that contain PHI, but for hosted customers that may increase costs and requires explicit agreement in the contract.

- Certifications & BAA: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 (evidence available). Legal is typically able to execute a BAA for customers with PHI — I'll loop in Security/Legal for a standard BAA template.

Attachments: observr_telemetry_sla.pdf (excerpt), redwood_subprocessors_matrix.xlsx (already in thread).

Let me know if you want short, copy-paste bullets for procurement.

Thanks,

Hi Alice / procurement team — thanks for the questions. Quick answers and next steps below (I copied Dev's bullets):

1) Subprocessors & telemetry
- Observr Inc. handles telemetry/metrics. CloudProviderX (GCP) is our cloud provider for compute/storage. See attached redwood_subprocessors_matrix.xlsx and an excerpt of the Observr SLA (observr_telemetry_sla.pdf).
- We can disable customer-level telemetry for BlueSky. We can also enable a strict redaction profile to ensure SDK/client logs do not contain PHI before any telemetry is sent.

2) Residency & deployment recommendation
- For strict EU-only PHI processing we recommend Redwood Private (customer-managed VPC or on-prem). Dedicated capacity in an EU region is a second option if you want managed infra + contractual residency guarantees. Hosted API can be constrained to EU data planes in some cases but is not our default for PHI.

3) Retention
- Log retention is configurable per-tenant and we can set retention to 7 years for buckets containing PHI. We'll need to include the retention clause in the contract and agree on associated costs.

4) Certifications & BAA
- Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001. We are willing to execute a BAA; I'll introduce Legal/Security to procurement once you share your questionnaire.

5) Marketplace & procurement flow
- We support marketplace purchasing through GCP Marketplace for many customers; please confirm whether you want to pursue marketplace licensing or a direct contract.

Next steps:
- Can we schedule a 30-minute follow-up Tue 26 May at 10:00 PT to review the subprocessor matrix and deployment options? If that works, I'll send a calendar invite.
- Please share procurement's questionnaire; I'll assign Legal/Security to respond.
